from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine coordinate grids as flexible, interactive rubber sheets.",
            "Linear transformations stretch or rotate this grid space.",
            "Vectors are simply arrows pointing within this space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The 'Digital Puppet'", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        # 1. Wireframe character (simple stick figure for demo)
        head = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#00FF00")
        body = Line(DOWN*0.5, UP*0.5, color="#00FF00")
        arms = Line(LEFT*0.5, RIGHT*0.5, color="#00FF00").shift(UP*0.3)
        puppet = VGroup(head, body, arms)
        puppet_label = Text("Wireframe", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        
        # 2. Rotation indicator
        rot_arrow = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color="#FF00FF")
        rot_label = Text("Rotation", font_size=18, color="#FF00FF")
        
        # 3. Vector
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5 + UP*1, color="#00FFFF")
        vec_label = Text("Coordinates", font_size=18, color="#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.place_in_area(puppet, 'B1', 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(puppet_label, 'A2')
        self.play(Create(puppet), Write(puppet_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.place_at_grid(rot_arrow, 'C5')
        self.place_at_grid(rot_label, 'B5')
        self.play(Create(rot_arrow), Write(rot_label))
        self.play(Rotate(puppet, angle=PI/6, about_point=self.grid['C2']))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(vector, 'D4', 'E6')
        self.place_at_grid(vec_label, 'F5')
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector), Write(vec_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Basis Vectors: The DNA of Transformation", [

            "The i-hat vector defines the grid's horizontal shift.",

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Matrix as a Transformation Recipe", [
            "A 2x2 matrix encodes these basis vector movements.",
            "Each column represents the new landing basis vector.",
            "Matrix multiplication tracks where every vector lands."
        ])
        
        # Define visual elements
        matrix = MathTex(r"M = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1.5 \end{bmatrix}", color=WHITE)
        col_1 = MathTex(r"v_1 = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}", color="#00FF00")
        col_2 = MathTex(r"v_2 = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1.5 \end{bmatrix}", color="#00FF00")
        transformation = MathTex(r"M \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1.5 \end{bmatrix}", color="#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(matrix))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(col_1, 'D2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(col_2, 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(col_1), Write(col_2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(transformation, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(transformation))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Dynamic Visualization: Rotation and Shear", [
            "Different matrices create distinct spatial effects easily.",
            "Rotation matrices turn the space around the origin.",
            "Shear matrices tilt the space while keeping lines parallel."
        ])

        # Grid and Unit vectors
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        rot_label = Text("Rotation", color="#0000FF", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(rot_label, 'B4')
        
        # Rotating grid
        self.play(grid.animate.rotate(PI/2, about_point=self.grid['C5']), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF7F00")
        
        shear_label = Text("Shear", color="#FF7F00", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(shear_label, 'D4')
        
        # Shear transformation
        shear_matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        self.play(grid.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Linear transformations preserve the origin and grid lines.",
            "Matrices act as compact recipes for spatial deformation.",
            "Geometry and algebra are now perfectly linked."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        grid_lines = VGroup(*[Line(start=[-3, -3, 0], end=[3, -3, 0]).shift(i * UP) for i in range(7)],
                            *[Line(start=[-3, -3, 0], end=[-3, 3, 0]).shift(i * RIGHT) for i in range(7)]).set_stroke(width=1)
        grid_morphed = grid_lines.copy().apply_matrix([[1, 1], [0, 1]]).set_stroke(color="#00FF00")
        
        matrix_eq = MathTex(r"A", r"\vec{x}", "=", r"\vec{b}").scale(1.5)
        summary_label = Text("Summary", color="#FFFFFF")
        concept_label = Text("Core Concept", color="#FFFF00")
        linear_space_label = Text("Linear Space", color="#CCCCCC")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(summary_label, "A3")
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_lines), FadeIn(summary_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(concept_label, "B3")
        self.place_in_area(matrix_eq, "D2", "D5")
        self.play(Transform(grid_lines, grid_morphed), FadeIn(matrix_eq), FadeIn(concept_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#CCCCCC")
        self.place_at_grid(linear_space_label, "E3")
        self.play(FadeIn(linear_space_label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometry of Linear Transformations: Mapping Space with Matrices

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Digital Puppet'
sections.content: Introduce linear transformations as a transformation of a 2D coordinate grid. Use the analogy of a rubber sheet being stretched or rotated. Define the prerequisite: vectors as arrows (x, y).
sections.example: A 2D character avatar on a screen stretching its arms—visualize the grid squares deforming while remaining parallel and equally spaced.

sections.title: The Basis Vectors: The DNA of Transformation
sections.content: Explain that any transformation is defined by where the basis vectors (i-hat: [1,0] and j-hat: [0,1]) land. If i-hat moves to [a,c] and j-hat moves to [b,d], the transformation is fully captured.
sections.example: Animate i-hat (red arrow) moving to (2, 0) and j-hat (green arrow) moving to (0, 1.5). Show the grid morphing into a rectangle.

sections.title: The Matrix as a Transformation Recipe
sections.content: Formalize the concept: The columns of a 2x2 matrix are the landing spots of our basis vectors. Multiplying a vector by a matrix is simply tracking where that vector's 'components' land in the new space.
sections.example: Represent the transformation [2, 0; 0, 1.5] acting on a vector [1, 1]. Show the math: 1*[2, 0] + 1*[0, 1.5] = [2, 1.5].

sections.title: Dynamic Visualization: Rotation and Shear
sections.content: Demonstrate that different matrices create different spatial effects. Introduce specific matrices for 90-degree rotation vs. 'shearing' (tilting).
sections.example: Animate a cat icon: Applying a shear matrix [1, 1; 0, 1] causes the cat to tilt sideways as if hit by a breeze, keeping its paws on the floor.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Linear transformations preserve origin and grid lines. The matrix is just a compact, numerical 'map' of the geometric deformation.
sections.example: A final 5-second animation overlaying a static 'input' grid with a morphed 'output' grid, showing the matrix equation linking the two.
